events.name: Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games - Team Event
events.coverage: India's men's and women's team-event matches. Singapore did not enter the team event.

sources.label: Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games - Men's team (Wikipedia)
Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games - Women's team (Wikipedia)

events.notes: Level set to MAJOR by analogy with the Olympics/World Championships tier in rules.json; the Asian Games isn't a BWF Tour event so it has no official tier name of its own. Team entries (MT/WT) replace the earlier per-discipline entries; rubbers are recorded inside each tie, not as separate entries. Men's team: India beat Bangladesh (R16) and Japan (QF), lost to China (SF) and won bronze; per this bracket format (byes=yes, no third-place match shown) semifinal losers are awarded bronze directly. Women's team: India beat Kazakhstan (R16), lost to Japan (QF) and were eliminated without a medal (only semifinal losers medal in this format). Neither bracket used a group stage; both were straight knockout with byes for the top 4 seeds, so no G1/G2/G3 ties apply this edition. Un-played rubbers after a tie was already decided are marked NOT_PLAYED, matching the 'np' cells on the source scoreboards. Singapore did not enter either squad list, confirming the team event has no Singaporean entries.

events.name: 2026 Suhandinata Cup
events.coverage: India's and Singapore's mixed-team results in the Suhandinata Cup (the World Junior Championships team event). The event uses a subgroup round robin, then a group play-off to settle 1st-8th in each of 8 groups, then a knockout ranking stage (5-11 October, both finishing and losing teams keep playing classification ties). Individual rubber scores are not published on the source page for the group-stage ties, only each tie's overall 2-set or 3-set result, so rubbers are omitted.
events.notes: India finished 2nd of 8 teams in Group D (won subgroup D1 over Algeria and Peru, then lost the group play-off to UAE); Singapore finished 2nd of 3 in subgroup B1 (beat Austria, lost to Czech Republic, then lost the second-placed play-off to Canada). Both continue in the event's classification/ranking knockout stage through 10 October, but the source had not yet published those pairings as of the read date.

events.notes: Squash has no third-place match, so no 3P match is recorded: both losing semifinalists take bronze and their runs end at SF. The men's singles page still shows a 3rd/4th result (Noor Zaman beat Muhammad Irfan, both PAK) that contradicts its own medal list; it involves no IND or SGP entry and is left out. First-round byes are not recorded as matches. The pages give a schedule by round, not by match, so each match date is its round's scheduled date and time is null (the 15:00 and similar times on the pages are session starts). Seeds are null for mixed doubles (the page shows bands such as 3/4) and for Au Yeong Wai Lynn and Au Yeong Wai Yhann (the women's singles page swaps their seeds 9 and 13 between rounds). Opponent names are as the pages display them (for example Muhammad Irfan, Tse Yee Lam Toby). Scores are left empty for the mixed doubles round of 16 between Joshna Chinappa/Velavan Senthilkumar and Suraj Chand/Shameena Riaz (page: 11-7, 11-10) and for the Chinappa/Senthilkumar semifinal loss to Lee Ka Yi/Tang Ming Hong (page: 10-11, 11-2, 10-11), because games ending 11-10 break the 11-point, win-by-2 game law the validator applies; the outcomes follow the bracket. The Singapore pair's round of 32 win over Khulan Purevjav/Amartuvshin Mandakhbayar is shown 11-0, 11-0; the page does not call it a walkover, so it is recorded as played.
